newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-GREEN HOMER, FIVE-HIT PITCHING LIFT JAYS PAST BREWERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GREEN HOMER, FIVE-HIT PITCHING LIFT JAYS PAST BREWERS.

text.p: Shawn Green's three-run homer in the seventh inning made a five-hitter by Pat Hentgen and two Toronto Blue Jay relievers good enough for a a 5-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers Tuesday.
Matt Mieske's solo homer in the top of the seventh off Hentgen gave Milwaukee a 2-1 edge, but the Jays answered with four runs in their half of the inning, capped by Green's blast.
"It felt good because it came at a crucial time with Pat Hentgen throwing such a great game," Green said. "It would've been tough to lose that after he gave up only the two runs."
Green is batting .412 (21-for-51) with five homers and 12 RBI in his last 12 games.
Dave Nilsson homered in the sixth to tie it for Milwaukee.
"The home runs were all we got. He's (Hentgen) a good pitcher, period," Brewers manager Phil Garner said. "He was a Cy Young pitcher last year. But everyone looks like Cy Young against our offence."
Hentgen (10-7) allowed two runs and four hits with two walks and six strikeouts. Dan Plesac got the final out of the eighth. Kelvim Escobar pitched the ninth for his third save.
"Early on I struggled a bit, then I got in a good groove," Hentgen said. "I made a few mistakes, to Nilsson and Mieske obviously, then Green hit the big home run. He was the story tonight."
Cal Eldred (9-10) limited Toronto to three runs -- two earned -- and two hits over six innings.
In New York, Andy Pettitte pitched 6 2/3 innings to win his fourth straight start and the Yankees scored three times in both the first and ninth innings in a 7-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Pettitte (12-5) allowed nine hits, walked one and struck out three. He gave up a run-scoring single to Kelly Stinnett in the sixth that pulled the Brewers within 4-3. But Pettitte nabbed Stinnett off first base for his league-leading 11th pickoff and retired Fernando Vina on a lineout.
Mike Stanton recorded the final five outs, striking out two, to earn his first save since June 6, 1996, when he was with the Red Sox.
Bryce Florie (1-2) lost in his first major-league start.

In Cleveland, David Justice snapped a sixth-inning tie with a two-run homer off Jeff Fassero (8-6) and the Indians got four scoreless innings from their bullpen en route to a 6-2 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
It was the first homer for the Indians in 47 innings. Since being activated from the disabled list on June 10, Justice has hit in 10 of 12 games, going 15-for-48 (.312)

David Weathers (1-1) threw two scoreless innings in relief of starter Orel Hershiser, who held the Mariners hitless for 4 2/3 innings before giving up consecutive homers to Russ Davis and Jose Cruz Jr. He left with a strained right groin.
Paul Assenmacher retired one batter in the eighth and Mike Jackson struck out three of the five batters he faced for his 14th save.

At Texas, Jeffrey Hammonds tied a career high with four hits and Rafael Palmeiro and Brady Anderson each drove in three runs as the Baltimore Orioles coasted to a 9-3 victory over the slumping Rangers.

Scott Erickson (12-5) snapped his three-start winless streak, allowing one run and nine hits over 5 1/3 innings. Arthur Rhodes held the Rangers scoreless through 3 1/3 innings. Alan Mills got the final out.
Rafael Palmeiro homered in the first off John Burkett (7-9), who yielded six runs and nine hits over 1 2/3 innings.
Texas has lost seven of its last nine.

In Boston, Jeff Frye's third hit of the game, an RBI single with two out in the eighth inning, scored pinch-runner Jesus Tavarez with the go-ahead run as the Boston Red Sox edged the Oakland Athletics 4-3.
Frye, playing more due to Tim Naehring's season-ending surgery, scored Boston's first run after leading off the third with a double.

Frye, who learned after the game that his wife is expecting the couple's second child, had an infield single in the fourth to drive in the third Red Sox run. Since the All-Star break, Frye is 16-for-46 (.348).
Oakland has lost four straight.
In Detroit, Tony Clark and Bobby Higginson homered and Brian Moehler (7-8) pitched six solid innings as the Tigers defeated the Chicago White Sox 6-3.
Danny Darwin (4-8) gave up five runs and seven hits in 2 2/3 innings, his shortest start of the season.

In Minnesota, Marty Cordova singled and scored the go-ahead run on a groundout by Darrin Jackson to snap a seventh-inning tie and lift the Twins to a season-high fifth straight victory, 3-2 over the Kansas City Royals.
